Subject: Renewal conversation — looking for a structure that smooths spend across BUs

Hi Sofia,

Quick note as we start planning FY25: our three business units will be renewing at different cadences, and procurement asked whether Redwood can offer a single contract that smooths commit across the year while still allowing BU-level ramp flexibility. Ideally we'd avoid multiple amendments and keep a single PO.

Key asks:
- Multi-year option (24–36 months) with an ability to front-load credits if needed.
- A mechanism to move committed capacity between BUs within a term without full legal amendments.
- Some form of tiled ramping so spend doesn't spike in Q1.

Can you share a few structured options we can present to procurement (and a rough example schedule)? Attaching our current utilization summary.

Thanks — Julia

Julia Park
Head of Platform Ops, Apex Analytics

Julia — thanks for the context and the usage summary, that helps. I've sketched three pragmatic options below and attached a one-pager + ramp schedule example. High-level: we can accomplish your goal with a "tiling" approach (time-boxed capacity tiles) combined with phase gates tied to business milestones, which avoids legal churn while giving BU flexibility.

Option A — 24m blended commit (single PO)
- One master contract for 24 months, billed quarterly.
- Commit divided into 4 equal "tiles" (each 6 months). Each BU can draw from tiles; we provide an internal transfer request process (no amendment) up to 20% of tile volume per quarter.
- Auto-renew default: opt-in per BU at tile boundaries.
- Price: blended unit rate with early front-load credit option.

Option B — 36m staircase (predictable unit-rate reductions)
- 36-month term with pre-agreed ramp milestones (phase-gates) at months 6, 12, 24.
- If utilization hits milestone X, next tile unlocks at a discounted rate; otherwise remains at baseline.
- Allows Apex to have capacity headroom without immediate spend.

Option C — Annual co-terming via internal credits
- Annual financial co-term for billing only; legal contract for 36 months.
- We issue internal credits for unused volume that can be reallocated to other BUs (requires sign-off from procurement but avoids full contract redline).

I've attached: "Redwood - Apex Renewal Options v1.pdf" and an example "Apex_ramp_schedule.xlsx" with a proposed tiling calendar.

Next steps I suggest: 1) choose which option to model; 2) we do a short call with procurement and finance to validate PO flow; 3) draft a term sheet.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday or Friday?

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Thanks for the call earlier — productive. Recap and agreed next steps below (short and actionable).

Recap of decisions made on the call:
- Apex selects Option A (24m blended commit) with tile architecture. Tiles sized quarterly for easier PO mapping (6 tiles over 24 months).
- Internal transfer: up to 25% per tile without legal; up to 50% with AM approval and a simple e-sign addendum (no redline).
- Front-load credits: Apex will take a one-time front-load credit equivalent to 10% of year-1 committed spend applied to tile 1 only.
- Billing cadence: quarterly invoicing with monthly true-up reports. Finance requested a PO line for "Reserved Inference Credits — Redwood Inference".
- Auto-renew: contract auto-renews at master level; BU-level opt-in at each tile boundary. Procurement asked to make opt-in explicit in the term sheet.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Sofia: produce a draft term sheet reflecting the tile calendar + transfer rules — deliver by Tue 12/7. (attachment: HubSpot-Deal-12345-summary.pdf)
